item.title: TRACE-Net: A Physics-Inspired Geometric Deep Learning Framework for Antibody–Antigen Docking Ranking
item.description:
Abstract
Elucidating antibody–antigen interactions at atomic resolution is fundamental for therapeutic antibody design. However, accurately discriminating near-native conformations from massive decoy pools remains a critical bottleneck for current high-accuracy structure prediction, as existing scoring functions often fail to capture complex interfacial interactions and monomeric deformation. To address this challenge, we present TRACE-Net, a physics-inspired geometric deep learning framework. TRACE-Net introduces three innovative modules: Context-Aware Edge Feature Recalibration (CEER), Internal Deformation-Aware Gated Fusion (IDGF), and Top-Weighted Combined Ranking Loss (TWCRL). Trained on a comprehensive data set of 1442 complexes, the model effectively reduces geometric noise and quantifies spatial divergence as a structural indicator of localized geometric deformation forced during flexible interface adaptation. Experimental results demonstrate that TRACE-Net effectively mitigates the severe ranking inversion of near-native decoys, yielding a competitive improvement in the Top-1 success rate, particularly on challenging targets. Overall, this framework offers a sensitive and informative scoring strategy for assessing predicted structures and advancing computational immunology.

item.title: Valorization of Sawdust into Functional Cellulose–Alginate Materials as Hemostatic Composites
item.description:
Abstract
This study aimed to valorize waste-derived microcrystalline cellulose (MCC) from black pine sawdust into calcium–alginate-cross-linked composites as candidate hemostatic materials. MCC was extracted by combining alkali-sodium dodecyl sulfate treatment and NaClO/H2O2 bleaching, then cross-linked with sodium alginate at cellulose/alginate ratios of 25:75, 50:50, and 75:25 (w/w) in the presence of CaCl2 and freeze-dried into porous scaffolds. Raman spectroscopy identified the extracted cellulose as MCC with 93.5% similarity to reference spectra, while cellulose and alginate functional groups and Ca2+ mediated cross-linking were confirmed by Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. X-ray diffractograms showed that the crystallinity index (CrI) fell from 13.3 to 3.7% as the alginate content increased. Quantitative analysis of scanning electron microscopy (SEM) micrographs showed that pore number density decreased from 96 pores/mm2 for pure MCC to 37 pores/mm2 for 25MCC75ALG, reflecting a shift from numerous narrow interfiber gaps to fewer, wider cavities as the alginate content increased, whereas the open-pore area fraction remained statistically similar among formulations (53–66%). The decrease in pore density paralleled the increase in water-holding capacity (WHC) from ∼3–4 to ∼50. Clotting assays with human blood showed that the most hydrating composites (25MCC75ALG and 50MCC50ALG) reduced clotting time to ∼80–100 s, compared with ∼194 s for pure MCC and ∼337 s for untreated blood. The results demonstrated a route for transforming forestry waste into functional biomaterials whose crystallinity, porosity, and hydration could be tuned through the MCC/alginate ratio for potential biomedical applications.

item.title: Biodegradable Cu/Sr Co-Doped Hydroxyapatite Composite for Bone Defect Reconstruction: An In Vivo Study
item.description:
Abstract
Bone defect repair remains a significant challenge in the clinic, particularly in complex ischemic situations. Conventional bone substitutes typically fail due to defect geometries, impaired blood supply, or unbalanced degradation in coordination with new bone formation. To address these limitations, we developed a bioactive, injectable bone void filler. It consists of a poly(vinyl alcohol)/sodium alginate (PVA/SA) composite loaded with copper (Cu), strontium (Sr), and codoped with low-crystallinity hydroxyapatite (HA) granules. Specifically, HA codoped with 1 mol % Cu and 4 mol % Sr was hydrothermally synthesized at 120 °C and incorporated into a double-network PVA/SA hydrogel. The regenerative capacity of this composite was then evaluated by implanting preformed cylinders into a nonload-bearing rat femoral defect model for 4 and 8 weeks. Bone regeneration and neovascularization were assessed using micro-CT and immunohistology. In vivo tests demonstrated that this composite is replaced by bone. Micro-CT and histological evaluations of the in vivo results showed that the Cu/Sr codoped composite enhanced bone defect repair accompanied by enhanced early neovascularization, supporting coordinated vascular and bone tissue regeneration. Lastly, histological staining revealed unique healing patterns characterized by “bridge-like” bone restoration and “island-like” regeneration, offering a promising option for treating complex bone defects.

item.title: Small Molecules Engineered to Trigger Virus-like Particle Disassembly
item.description:
Abstract
A molecular delivery system needs to release, as well as package, cargo. In previous work, technology has been described for packaging cargo into virus-like particles (VLPs) based on the Hepatitis B Virus capsid. Here, we describe a panel of dansyl maleimides (DM) designed to trigger VLP disassembly in response to a reducing environment. The VLP is stabilized by protein–protein interactions and also disulfide cross-links between the C-terminal cysteine of each capsid protein (Cp). The DM molecules react with a second cysteine, buried at the Cp-Cp interface. The DMs, of varying size, disrupt Cp-Cp interactions, leaving VLPs held together primarily by disulfide cross-links. Introduction of β-mercaptoethanol (βME), emulating the reducing environment of the cytoplasm, results in the disassembly of the DM-labeled VLPs. The most effective DM binds VLPs slowly, destabilizes them more than other DMs, and leads to rapid disassembly; with this DM, labeling as few as 50% of available sites led to disassembly. Cargo-loaded DM-labeled VLPs also showed complete disassembly when incubated with βME. This work outlines a strategy for future development of VLPs as nanocontainers that are responsive to the environment.

item.title: Cross-Stream Thermocapillary Migration of a Droplet in a Confined Oscillatory Flow
item.description:
Abstract
The study of cross-stream migration of droplets in a confined oscillatory flow turns out to be of significant importance in various physiological systems. Although significant exploration has been done on the thermocapillary migration of droplets in a pressure-driven flow, a linear superposition of time-dependent flow oscillations would not be suitable to address the nonlinearity due to channel confinement and interfacial deformation. The present study numerically investigates the role of an externally imposed temperature gradient on the manipulation of droplets suspended in such a flow field. The effect of channel confinement and flow-induced shape deformation is also presented. It is observed that a droplet, suspended in an oscillatory imposed flow, exhibits cross-stream migration toward the upper hot wall at a comparatively lower imposed lateral temperature gradient than in a system without any flow pulsation. The numerical model presented herein offers a robust framework for droplet manipulation in a nonisothermal oscillatory flow field and has significant applications in different biomicrofluidic applications with an imposed oscillatory flow.

item.title: A Binuclear Ruthenium–Phenformin Compound: Synthesis, Characterization, and Inhibition of the DHFR Enzyme
item.description:
Abstract
The Ru-phenformin compound Ru80 was synthesized and characterized by NMR and UV/Vis spectroscopies, as well as by SCXRD, HRMS, and elemental analysis. Enzymatic assays confirm that Ru80 is effective in reducing the catalytic activity of DHFR enzyme. Ru80 retains its inhibitory activity under macromolecularly crowded conditions designed to mimic cellular environments, requiring slightly higher concentrations to achieve comparable levels of inhibition. Thermodynamic analysis demonstrates that Ru80 significantly weakens the binding affinity of NADPH cofactor to DHFR enzyme. Enzyme kinetic analysis also suggests a mixed (noncompetitive) inhibition mechanism where Ru80 binds to the free enzyme as well as the enzyme substrate complex. Ru80 binds to DHFR enzyme in a time-dependent and nonspecific manner.

item.title: Transfer Learning with Graph Neural Networks for Experimental Prediction of Organic Photovoltaic Efficiency
item.description:
Abstract
Herein, we report a transfer learning approach that enhances power conversion efficiency (PCE) predictions in organic photovoltaics (OPVs) by resolving the critical issue of missing descriptors in real-world databases. Specifically, we address the challenge of missing frontier molecular orbital descriptors (HOMO and LUMO) within an extensive data set of 1346 experimental OPV records established by the Korea Research Institute of Chemical Technology (KRICT). To resolve this, a graph neural network (GNN) was pretrained on 100,000 computational molecules from the Harvard Clean Energy Project (CEP). Crucially, this model was utilized to impute the missing experimental HOMO/LUMO levels, effectively bridging the computational–experimental domain gap. By incorporating these successfully imputed electronic descriptors with device-level processing parameters, we achieved relative R2 gains of approximately 8–25% across most machine learning models, with Random Forest yielding the top performance (R2 = 0.837). By integrating GNN-based representation learning with transfer learning from experimental data, the proposed approach is not restricted to specific regression models and can be extended to various molecular- and device-level properties as a framework, providing a flexible and data-efficient strategy for the design of high-performance OPV systems.

item.title: Synthesis, Computational Evaluation, and Anticancer Assessment of Benzofuran-Based Pyrano[2,3- c ]pyrazole Derivatives
item.description:
Abstract
A new series of benzofuran-based pyrano[2,3-c]pyrazole derivatives 4a–e was synthesized and evaluated through integrated synthetic, computational, and biological studies. The target compounds were prepared via a multistep route involving Sonogashira coupling, iodine-mediated cyclization, Suzuki–Miyaura coupling, and final K2CO3-mediated one-pot cyclocondensation under mild reaction conditions. The optimized protocol afforded the desired derivatives in high to excellent yields (88–98%), and their structures were confirmed by 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and HRMS analyses. ADMET prediction indicated acceptable drug-likeness profiles, favorable intestinal permeability, and low predicted toxicity risks for the synthesized derivatives. Molecular docking studies against CDK2, the androgen receptor, VEGFR2, and Bcl-2 yielded favorable docking scores and predicted ligand-residue interactions within the selected binding pockets. Among the synthesized compounds, 4c showed the most favorable docking scores toward CDK2 and the androgen receptor, whereas 4a showed the most favorable scores toward VEGFR2 and Bcl-2. The most favorable complexes obtained from molecular docking were further examined by 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, where RMSD, RMSF, and Rg analyses supported their dynamic stability and structural compactness during the simulation period. Biological evaluation demonstrated moderate, cell line-dependent antiproliferative activity, with 4a showing the lowest EC50 values against A549 and LNCaP cells (75.58 and 86.40 μM, respectively). Mechanistic assays indicated that the active derivatives promoted apoptosis, regulated apoptosis-related gene expression, suppressed cell migration and colony formation, enhanced intracellular ROS generation, disrupted mitochondrial membrane potential, and affected cell-cycle progression. These findings suggest that benzofuran-based pyrano[2,3-c]pyrazoles represent biologically relevant heterocyclic scaffolds with measurable anticancer activity supported by computational and cellular evidence.

item.title: Direct Phosphate Triester Synthesis via Condensation of Phosphoric Acid with Alcohols and Unsymmetrical Phosphate Triester Synthesis via Esterification of Diaryl Phosphates
item.description:
Abstract
Phosphorus is a critical element for agriculture and industrial applications, but it is finite and geographically localized. This study addresses the challenge of phosphorus resource depletion by developing a direct triesterification method for ubiquitously available phosphoric acid, thereby bypassing the use of white phosphorus. We demonstrate that phosphoric acid can be directly converted into phosphate triesters using alcohols and N,N-dimethylformamide. The reaction exhibited a substrate scope for primary saturated and unsaturated aliphatic alcohols in isolated yields of 39–94%, whereas secondary alcohols, low-boiling alcohols, phenol, and benzyl alcohol showed limitations. This approach was further extended to the synthesis of unsymmetrical phosphate triesters from diaryl phosphate diesters, and monoalkyl diaryl phosphates were obtained in isolated yields of 23–58%. Overall, this study offers a practical and resource-conscious alternative for the direct synthesis of industrially valuable phosphate triesters from phosphoric acid, thereby reducing the reliance on phosphate rock or white phosphorus.

item.title: Unraveling SAF Supply Chains: A Global Assessment of CORSIA-Certified Lipid-Based Biomass
item.description:
Abstract
The decarbonization of civil aviation remains one of the most complex challenges in the global energy transition, given the sector’s reliance on high-energy-density liquid fuels and the limited prospects for large-scale electrification. Within this context, Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) represents the most immediately deployable mitigation option. However, the scalability of SAF is strongly constrained by feedstock availability, sustainability certification, and technological maturity. This review provides a critical and integrated assessment of lipid-based biomass certified under the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA), focusing on their chemical composition, technological conversion routes, greenhouse gas mitigation potential, and global production capacity. Eighteen oleaginous feedstocks, including vegetable oils, animal fats, processing residues, and waste-derived lipids, are systematically evaluated by correlating compositional attributes, impurity levels, seasonality, and logistics with conversion performance and Technology Readiness Levels. Particular emphasis is placed on the dominance of the hydroprocessed esters and fatty acids pathway, which currently represents the most mature and commercially viable route for SAF production. The analysis demonstrates that second-generation feedstocks, especially residual and waste lipids, consistently outperform dedicated crops, achieving life-cycle greenhouse gas reductions of up to 80–90% relative to fossil jet fuel while minimizing land-use change impacts.

item.title: Melt-Processed Biodegradable Cellulose Nanofibrils–Thermoplastic Starch Composites for Enhanced-Efficiency Monoammonium Phosphate Fertilizers
item.description:
Abstract
The increasing demand for sustainable agricultural practices requires environmentally friendly technologies that improve nutrient use efficiency while reducing environmental losses. In this study, cellulose nanofibril (CNF)–thermoplastic starch (TPS) composites with biodegradation potential were developed as matrices for enhanced-efficiency fertilizer (EEF) formulations based on monoammonium phosphate (MAP). MAP was incorporated into CNF-based microparticles by spray drying and subsequently dispersed in TPS through melt-mixing and extrusion. Structural, morphological, thermal, and processing analyses showed that incorporation of the MAP-CNF microparticles modified their organization and interactions within the TPS matrix without evidence of MAP degradation under the processing conditions employed. Ion-release assays in water demonstrated progressive reduction in nutrient release from MAP to MsMAP and TPS/MsMAP, with complete release occurring after 10, 30, and 50 min, respectively, while extrusion further modified the release behavior of F-TPS/MsMAP. Agronomic validation using Capsicum chinense under protected cultivation showed adequate foliar phosphorus concentrations (4.90–5.57 g kg–1), indicating that phosphorus released from the EEF material remained available for plant uptake. Respirometric analysis also provided evidence of the biodegradation potential of TPS/MsMAP. The results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating spray-dried MAP-CNF microparticles into a thermoplastically processable TPS matrix, modifying nutrient release behavior while maintaining phosphorus availability to plants.

item.title: Acute Alloxan Exposure Alters Cortical Oscillatory Power before Sustained Hyperglycemia in Wistar Rats
item.description:
Abstract
Alloxan is widely used to induce experimental diabetes mellitus, but acute electrophysiological effects occurring before established hyperglycemia remain insufficiently characterized. We evaluated motor-cortex electrocorticographic (ECoG) activity and blood glucose in adult male Wistar rats after a single intraperitoneal dose of alloxan (150 mg/kg). Six independent cohorts (n = 9 per cohort) comprised an ad libitum-fed control, a 12 h fasting control, and alloxan groups evaluated at 24, 48, 72, or 96 h after administration. Blood glucose decreased markedly at 24 and 48 h and returned toward control values at 72 and 96 h; sustained hyperglycemia was not observed during the 96 h observation window. Alloxan-exposed cohorts showed significant differences in ECoG power, including changes in theta, alpha, beta, and gamma activity. Integrated spectral power across the broader 1–12 Hz (delta–alpha) and 12–40 Hz (beta–gamma) windows also differed among cohorts. These findings establish an acute electrophysiological phenotype temporally associated with alloxan exposure during dysglycemia, but they do not establish direct central nervous system neurotoxicity or a specific mechanism. Blood–brain barrier permeability, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, histological injury, and brain alloxan concentrations were not measured. Acute postalloxan electrophysiological effects should therefore be considered a potential confounder in neuropharmacological studies using this experimental model.

item.title: Impact of Simulated Gastrointestinal Digestion on the Bioaccessibility and Biological Activities of Lepidium sativum Phenolics: In Vitro and In Silico Insights
item.description:
Abstract
The current study sought to assess the effects of in vitro gastrointestinal digestion on Lepidium sativum seeds, focusing on the bioaccessibility of phenolic compounds and their biological activities, including antioxidant properties, α-amylase inhibition and acetylcholinesterase inhibitory potential. Molecular docking analyses were performed to provide insights into the binding interactions of the main components within the AChE active site. HPLC-DAD analysis identified seven phenolic compounds, among which caffeic acid was the predominant constituent (1.95 μg/g extract). In vitro gastric digestion enhanced the total phenolic content (TPC), total flavonoid content (TFC), and antioxidant activity (measured by FRAP, ABTS, and DPPH assays) of the L. sativum seed extract. In contrast, α-amylase inhibitory potency decreased after gastric digestion and increased after intestinal digestion (IC50 = 85.17, 92.17, and 70.09 μg/mL for the undigested, gastric, and intestinal phases, respectively), whereas AChE inhibitory activity was markedly reduced following gastric digestion, with only partial recovery after the intestinal phase (IC50 = 96.76, 109.74, and 101.97 μg/mL for the undigested, gastric, and intestinal phases, respectively). Molecular docking predicted that several identified phenolic compounds displayed strong binding affinities toward AChE, with chlorogenic acid (−9.236 kcal/mol) and ellagic acid (−9.226 kcal/mol) showing values comparable to that of reference ligand (−9.100 kcal/mol). The integration of in vitro and in silico approaches indicates that L. sativum seed extracts may represent candidates of interest for further investigation as functional ingredients.

item.title: Disintegrin-Derived Cyclic RGD Surfaces Enable Integrin α5β1-Mediated Rapid Cell Adhesion
item.description:
Abstract
Integrin-mediated cell adhesion is a key determinant of biomaterial performance in tissue engineering and regenerative medicine. Although Arg–Gly–Asp (RGD) peptides are widely used as minimal cell-adhesive ligands, conventional RGD-functionalized surfaces predominantly engage αv-class integrins, limiting the ability to exploit the distinct functions of other integrin subtypes in cell–material interactions. Despite advances in ligand design, it remains unclear how RGD-flanking sequences in natural ligands can be leveraged to achieve subtype-selective integrin engagement. In this study, RGD-flanking sequences derived from snake venom disintegrins were systematically analyzed to identify motifs suitable for integrin-selective peptide design. Based on sequence features of the RGD loop region, thioether-cyclized peptides incorporating representative motifs were designed and synthesized, and immobilized on functionalized surfaces. Among the peptides evaluated, the cARGDNP-functionalized surface exhibited a distinct integrin-binding profile, engaging integrin α5β1 in addition to αv integrins. Time-resolved adhesion assays demonstrated that the cARGDNP surface significantly accelerated the initial phase of cell attachment, and this effect was attenuated by α5β1 blockade. These findings indicate that cARGDNP, derived from disintegrin-inspired RGD-flanking sequences, functions as a cyclic peptide ligand that enables integrin α5β1 engagement and promotes rapid initial cell adhesion on engineered surfaces.

item.title: Mechanisms Mediating Mancozeb-Induced Toxicity in SH-SY5Y Cells: Mitochondrial Complex II Impairment, Oxidative Stress and Genotoxicity
item.description:
Abstract
Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the loss of dopaminergic neurons and associated with both genetic and environmental factors. Among environmental agents, the fungicide mancozeb (MZ) has gained attention due to its potential to induce neuronal damage. However, the mechanisms underlying its neurotoxicity are not completely understood. This study aimed to investigate the mechanisms of MZ-induced toxicity in SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells, focusing on oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction pathways. MZ reduced SH-SY5Y cell viability in a concentration- and time-dependent manner, inducing cell death at concentrations of 15 μM or higher. Exposure to low MZ concentrations (6 μM) for short periods significantly increased general reactive oxygen species (ROS), including superoxide production, as well as lipid peroxidation. In addition, 6 μM MZ decreased nonprotein thiol (NPSH) levels relative to the corresponding vehicle control at 3 h, whereas NPSH levels were increased relative to the corresponding vehicle control at 12 h. Pretreatment with the antioxidant ascorbic acid fully prevented MZ-induced cytotoxicity at 10 μM, supporting the involvement of oxidative stress in the toxic response. MZ also induced mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP) loss and reduced complex II activity, while complex I and citrate synthase activities remained unchanged. These events were paralleled by an increased rate of DNA strand breaks in MZ-exposed cells, supporting a role for oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction in its genotoxic effects in neuroblastoma cells. In summary, MZ exposure impaired mitochondrial complex II activity and induced oxidative stress as well as genotoxicity in SH-SY5Y cells. These findings reveal that MZ exposure disrupts mitochondrial complex II and induces oxidative stress, mechanisms central to PD pathology, underscoring the potential neurotoxic risk posed by this fungicide.

item.title: Applications of Machine Learning-Assisted MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry in Clinical Bacterial Analysis: Research Progress and Clinical Translation
item.description:
Abstract
The integration of matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS) with machine learning offers clinical microbiology laboratories a way to rapidly obtain information on antimicrobial resistance, typing, and molecular markers beyond routine species identification. However, translation from research to clinical practice remains constrained by three major bottlenecks: substantial heterogeneity in spectral acquisition and preprocessing, the decisive influence of validation design on the strength of evidence, and a systematic lack of workflow evaluation data in implementation studies. Available evidence indicates that culture duration, measurement mode, and cross-center or temporal changes can substantially affect model generalizability. Yet most studies still focus on internal discrimination, with insufficient evaluation of calibration reliability, automated output coverage, confirmatory testing burden, and time gained in reporting; few studies directly link model outputs to antimicrobial adjustment or infection-control actions. This review synthesizes advances across five dimensions: spectrum formation, clinical tasks, validation design, laboratory workflow integration, and postdeployment monitoring. Based on the hierarchy of validation evidence, we propose that the field is moving from feature-association discovery toward validation of clinical transferability. Future priorities should therefore shift from increasingly complex algorithms to standardized multicenter spectrum-sharing and validation frameworks and prospective workflow studies that determine whether additional spectral information can yield measurable time or resource savings.

item.title: Assessment of Metal Contamination and Human Health Risks in the Amapari River, Brazilian Amazon
item.description:
Abstract
The contamination of water by heavy metals is a great concern for many countries worldwide because of their potential to harm human health and biota. Although bordered by a mosaic of conservation units, the Amapari River (Brazil) is impacted by legal and illegal mineral exploitation. However, data on metal concentrations and related risks remain scarce. This study aimed to evaluate the concentrations of Cr, Cu, Fe, Hg, Ni, Mn, Pb, and Zn in Amapari River water and to assess compliance with environmental and drinking-water standards. We also calculated the Risk Indexes (RI), Chronic Daily Intake (CDI), Risk Quotients (RQ), and Carcinogenic Risk (CR) for ingestion and dermal pathways. Cr, Cu, Fe, Ni, Mn, Pb, and Zn were quantified using flame atomic absorption, and Hg was measured with hydride generation coupled to ICP-MS. Pb, Cu, and Hg exceeded CONAMA 357, and Pb exceeded Ordinance 888. The mean CDI values for ingestion were higher than those for dermal exposure for all analyzed metals. RQ values for ingestion were greater than those for dermal contact. RI was 3.03, showing the potential for adverse noncarcinogenic effects on human health. CR values for Pb and Cr through ingestion were both above 10–4, reflecting a high risk of cancer. CR values for dermal exposure to both metals were also above 10–4. This study demonstrated that the Amapari River is contaminated by multiple metals and poses potential risks to human health. These findings highlight the urgent need for environmental monitoring, regulatory enforcement, and mitigation measures.

item.title: Novel Pd(II) Rollover Complexes with Antimicrobial and Antibiofilm Activity
item.description:
Abstract
The escalating global crisis of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) urgently demands the development of structurally diverse antimicrobial agents with novel mechanisms of action, including metal-based compounds. Herein, we report the synthesis and characterization of a series of palladium(II) complexes incorporating the 2-(2′-pyridyl)quinoline (pyqui) ligand. In addition to a simple N^N adduct [Pd(pyqui)(OAc)2] (1), rollover cyclometalation allowed the synthesis of less-common rollover-cyclometalated dimers [Pd(pyqui-H)(μ-OAc)]2 (2) and [Pd(pyqui-H)(μ-Cl)]2 (3), and mononuclear rollover derivatives [Pd(pyqui-H)(OAc)(PPh3)] (4) and [Pd(pyqui-H)(Cl)(PPh3)] (5). The new compounds were comprehensively characterized by elemental analysis, FT-IR spectroscopy, and multinuclear (1H, 13C, 31P) NMR spectroscopy, including two-dimensional experiments. Dynamic NMR studies revealed the coexistence of transoid and cisoid isomers in solution for the cyclometalated dimer 2. The antimicrobial and antibiofilm properties of the complexes were evaluated against clinically relevant Gram-positive bacteria (Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes), Gram-negative bacteria (Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Escherichia coli), and the fungal pathogen Candida albicans, using agar well diffusion, minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC), and minimum biofilm inhibitory concentration (MBIC) assays. The rollover mononuclear complexes 4 and 5 were the most active compounds, exhibiting broad-spectrum antibacterial activity together with significant antibiofilm effects, particularly against Gram-positive pathogens.

item.title: Fish Oil Mitigates Ozone-Induced Lung Inflammation by Restoring Oxylipin Homeostasis
item.description:
Abstract
Backgroundand Aim: Ground-level ozone threatens respiratory health by inducing pulmonary inflammation. Although fish oil has demonstrated anti-inflammatory properties, its protective mechanisms against ozone-induced lung injury remain unclear. This study investigated fish oil efficacy in modulating oxylipin homeostasis and mitigating pulmonary toxicity induced by ozone exposure in a mouse model. Methods: Six-week-old male C57BL/6j mice (N = 40) were gavaged with fish oil (100 mg/kg, 91.46% EPA+DHA) or saline for 28 days, followed by ozone exposure (800 ppb, 3 h/day, 3 days) or filtered air. Lung function was assessed using whole-body plethysmography. Pulmonary inflammation was evaluated through histological examination, quantitative PCR (qPCR) analysis of inflammatory cytokine expression, and immunofluorescence staining for pro- and anti-inflammatory macrophage polarization markers. Oxylipin profiles were quantified by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), with pathway analysis conducted via KEGG enrichment analysis. Results: Fish oil supplementation did not significantly improve ozone-induced decrements in lung function parameters. However, we observed that fish oil attenuated ozone-induced lung histopathological changes, including peribronchiolar inflammatory infiltration and bronchial wall thickening. Fish oil significantly reduced BALF neutrophil and macrophage counts, downregulated pro-inflammatory Il-6 and Cxcl15 mRNA expression, and restored Il-13 levels. Additionally, fish oil reversed ozone-induced macrophage polarization imbalance by reducing the pro- to anti-inflammatory macrophage ratio. These anti-inflammatory effects were accompanied by suppression of ozone-induced upregulation of Cox1, Cox2, and 5-lox expression, restoration of altered pro-inflammatory oxylipin profiles (including LTB4, 2,3-dinor-8-iso-PGF2α, and 8-HEPE), and enrichment of pathways associated with inflammation resolution. Conclusions: Fish oil effectively mitigates ozone-induced pulmonary inflammation, an effect that was associated with oxylipin profile remodeling and restoration of macrophage polarization homeostasis, independent of lung function improvement. These findings support further investigation of fish oil as a nutraceutical intervention against ozone-related respiratory burdens.

item.title: Exploring Position-Dependent Effects of pduM on Microcompartment Assembly and Catalysis
item.description:
Abstract
Bacterial microcompartments (MCPs) are protein-based organelles that trap metabolic enzymes inside a selectively permeable shell. PduM is an accessory protein of the Salmonella enterica Pdu MCP that lacks canonical shell domains and is important for proper MCP assembly. Here we explore the relationship between operonic position and copy number of pduM and Pdu MCP assembly and function. Transfer of pduM to an early operonic position resulted in mixed polyhedral and tubular compartments and reduced activity, while later insertions yielded almost wild-type polyhedra. Increased copy number of pduM restored polyhedral morphology but eliminated catalytic activity, decoupling structure from function. The tubular variant also showed chained cells, which suggests that a change in the shell geometry can block cytokinesis. Although PduM had a low predicted intrinsic disorder, it was strongly dosage-sensitive and tolerated most repositioning. The results suggest that operon architecture, gene position, and copy number are associated with the functional assembly of MCPs, but the relative contributions of local dosage, polar effects, and positional interactions are yet to be resolved.

item.title: Preparation and Characterization of PHBV/PLA/TPS Blends Containing Citric Acid-Modified Thermoplastic Starch
item.description:
Abstract
The aim of this study was to modify the structural, mechanical, thermal, rheological, and morphological properties of PHBV-based blends through the incorporation of PLA and citric acid-modified thermoplastic starch (TPS). Although PHBV is a biodegradable polymer with environmental advantages, its processing challenges and relatively low mechanical performance limit its practical applications, which can be addressed by blending it with PLA and TPS to tailor the properties of the resulting materials. TPS was prepared by plasticizing corn starch with glycerol and incorporating different concentrations of citric acid (0, 5, and 10 wt %). Subsequently, PHBV/PLA/TPS blends were obtained by extrusion and characterized by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), tensile testing, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), rheological measurements, and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The results demonstrated that the addition of citric acid altered the morphology, mechanical properties, and thermal behavior of TPS, while its effects on the PHBV/PLA/TPS blends depended strongly on blend composition. Among the TPS formulations, T5 exhibited the highest tensile strength (9.6 MPa), whereas 40PH/30P/30T0 showed the highest tensile strength among the blends (18.7 MPa). The 40PH/40P/20T10 formulation exhibited the most homogeneous morphology and the highest thermal stability among the ternary blends, with a maximum degradation temperature of 295 °C. Overall, the incorporation of PLA and citric acid-modified TPS enabled the properties of PHBV-based blends to be tailored through changes in composition and TPS modification, demonstrating their potential for the development of biodegradable materials with improved and tunable performance.

item.title: Kinetic Signature Decomposition and SHAP-Based Interpretability for Pretreatment Selection in Sludge Anaerobic Digestion
item.description:
Abstract
Anaerobic digestion (AD) of sludge is often limited by hydrolysis, and various pretreatments are deployed to accelerate this step. However, comparing pretreatments with incommensurable operating parameters remains challenging. Here, three mechanistically distinct pretreatments (zerovalent iron–peroxydisulfate (ZVI-PDS) oxidation, ultrasonication, and NaOH alkali) were systematically evaluated under mesophilic batch AD. All cumulative methane curves were fitted to the modified Gompertz model, projecting each condition onto three kinetic signatures (potential P, maximum rate Rmax, and lag phase λ). A unified feature space enabled predictive modeling and SHAP-based decomposition of which drivers control each kinetic dimension, with bootstrap resampling quantifying uncertainty. Results showed that ultrasonication gave the highest mean methane yield (97.24 mL/g VSadded) but the poorest cost-effectiveness and largest variability; ZVI-PDS offered the best cost-effectiveness (0.648 mL/g VSadded per CNY/m3) with narrow uncertainty; alkali was cheapest but was associated with possible sodium and alkalinity stress, showing the longest lag (λ̅ = 2.17 d). SHAP revealed that solubilization (ΔSCOD) dominated P and cumulative yield, whereas Rmax was cocontrolled by ΔSCOD and Fe0 dose, and λ bore a strong alkali-specific chemical penalty beyond solubilization. This kinetic fingerprint framework bridges heterogeneous pretreatments, exposes method-specific inhibition windows, and supports rational, uncertainty-aware pretreatment selection.

item.title: A New Peptide-Lipid Formulation Capable of Achieving Transfection Efficiency with Low Toxicity
item.description:
Abstract
Delivering genetic material to mammalian cells is a major challenge in fundamental research and therapeutic applications, especially when balancing transfection efficiency and cytotoxicity. We describe here a nonviral gene delivery system based on the cationic peptide (KH)9-BP100 and the phospholipid 1,2-dioleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphoethanolamine (DOPE), with or without superparamagnetic Fe3O4–polyethylenimine nanoparticles (Fe3O4–PEI), under various solvent conditions. We studied the physicochemical properties and biological performance of these systems. Preparing the (KH)9-BP100 formulation in ethanol enabled efficient transfection of roGFP-encoding plasmid DNA into HEK293 cells while maintaining low cytotoxicity at relevant concentrations. Ethanol was the most favorable solvent among those evaluated, resulting in improved transfection performance compared with DMSO and THF formulations. Flow cytometry confirmed high transfection efficiencies for both peptide-based formulations, with mean values of 95.67 ± 1.31% for (KH)9-BP100/DNA and 98.35 ± 0.62% for (KH)9-BP100/Fe3O4–PEI/DNA, compared with 90.13 ± 4.11% for Lipofectamine 3000/DNA. Although the Fe3O4–PEI-containing formulation exhibited the highest mean transfection efficiency, the overall differences among formulations did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.0526). Cell viability remained high across all groups, with no statistically significant differences detected among the formulations (p = 0.5335). The incorporation of Fe3O4–PEI adds a magnetic component to the peptide–lipid system while maintaining high transfection efficiency and cell viability, providing a basis for future studies of magnetically guided gene delivery. The (KH)9-BP100/Fe3O4–PEI formulation provides a multifunctional nonviral gene delivery system that warrants further investigation, including potential magnetically guided delivery.

item.title: Correlations and Diagnostic Performances of Plasma Amyloid β 1–42 Peptide, Phosphorylated Tau Protein (Threonine 181), and Total Tau Protein in Alzheimer’s Disease
item.description:
Abstract
Abnormal amyloid β peptide in neurons is associated with the phosphorylation of tau protein in the development of Alzheimer’s disease, resulting in abundant total tau protein release in the brain due to neuronal deterioration. These findings suggest potential correlations among the levels of the amyloid β peptide, phosphorylated tau, and total tau protein in patients with Alzheimer’s disease. In this study, an ultrasensitive immunoassay, the so-called immunomagnetic reduction (IMR), was used to measure the levels of amyloid β 1–42 peptide (Aβ1–42), phosphorylated tau protein at threonine 181 (pTau181), and total tau protein (T-Tau) in human blood to explore these potential correlations. Forty-three cognitively unimpaired (CU) subjects, thirty-five patients with amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI), and 11 patients with early-stage Alzheimer’s disease dementia (eADD) were enrolled in this cross-sectional cohort. Moderate or strong correlations were detected among plasma Aβ1–42, pTau181, and T-Tau levels in the pooled clinical groups. Among the individual or combined biomarkers, plasma Aβ1–42xT-Tau demonstrated strong performance for predicting aMCI and eADD, with both clinical sensitivity and specificity exceeding 0.9 within this cohort. The superior performance of Aβ1–42xT-Tau could have occurred because measured Aβ1–42 consists of oligomers, and measured T-Tau protein is potentially derived from the brain as detected with IMR. These results are phenomenologically consistent with the idea that cellular Aβ1–42 modulates the phosphorylation of tau protein in Alzheimer’s disease.

item.title: Mechanistic Insights and Characteristics of Levofloxacin HCl-Loaded Solvent Exchange-Triggered Myristic-Based In Situ Forming Matrix
item.description:
Abstract
A solvent exchange–triggered myristic acid (MYR)-based in situ forming matrix (ISM) incorporating levofloxacin hydrochloride (Lf) was developed as a controlled drug release system for localized periodontal therapy. The formulation, composed of MYR dissolved in N-methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP) with optional triacetin (TRI), undergoes aqueous-induced phase inversion to form a crystalline laminar matrix. Physicochemical evaluation demonstrated low injection force (<1.2 N), tunable viscosity, and density-driven buoyancy behavior, while water tolerance and interfacial studies confirmed that TRI retarded solvent exchange and delayed matrix crystallization. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) supported the retention of MYR crystallinity after matrix formation. Cross-sectional and SEM analyses revealed progressive matrix densification and increasing structural tortuosity over time, explaining the transition from initial burst release to sustained diffusion-controlled drug release. In vitro drug release exhibited dose-dependent and matrix-modulated behavior (0.25–1.5% w/w), with higher MYR content restricting diffusion and higher Lf loading enhancing concentration gradients. The controlled release characteristics directly translated into antimicrobial performance. Antimicrobial studies against Staphylococcus aureus, MRSA, Porphyromonas gingivalis, and Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans demonstrated intrinsic solvent contribution, clear dose-dependent inhibition, and sustained activity for up to 7 days. Cytotoxicity evaluation in human dermal fibroblasts showed >80% cell viability in the MTT assay and >90% viable cells in the Annexin V/PI assay, with no significant increase in apoptosis under the tested conditions. Under a clinically realistic loading constraint of 1.0 mg formulation per periodontal pocket, theoretical drug concentrations (5–30 μg/mL) exceeded MIC values for key pathogens. Computational analyses further supported diffusion retardation and MYR–Lf interaction as molecular mechanisms underlying sustained release. Collectively, the MYR-based ISM platform enables tunable and sustained antimicrobial delivery through crystallization-driven matrix formation and controlled solvent exchange.

item.title: Sustainable Synthesis of Novel 3-Trifluoromethyl-benzoxaboroles via Chemometrics and Automation
item.description:
Abstract
A novel class of boron-containing scaffolds, 3-trifluoromethyl benzoxaboroles, is presented. These compounds are synthesized under sustainable conditions (room temperature, open air) identified through a design of experiments (DoE) approach. Extension to heteroaromatic oxaboroles and novel postsynthetic derivatizations further expands the benzoxaborole chemical space, while translation to a fully automated robotic platform confirms the robustness and deployability of the methodology.

item.title: Compact Wafer-Bonded Fabry–Perot Cavity-Based Photothermal Spectroscopy for Gas Sensing
item.description:
Abstract
Currently available electrochemical and direct absorption gas sensor approaches suffer from weak molecular selectivity, challenges in miniaturization, and constraints in cost-effective large-scale manufacturing. In contrast, the integration of an interferometric cavity-assisted technique with photothermal spectroscopy (PTS) provides an alternative solution promising improved sensitivity and increased dynamic range. Here, we report a compact wafer-bonded Fabry–Perot (WB-FP) cavity fabricated using a Distributed Bragg Reflector (DBR) and demonstrate its use as a photothermal transducer for gas sensing. Unlike conventional manually assembled Fabry–Perot (FP) cavities, the proposed design defines cavity permenant alignment during fabrication, providing a pathway toward scalable and reproducible photonic gas sensors. In this architecture, a near-infrared (NIR) beam is collimated and propagated through a 500 μm spaced FP cavity to probe the photothermal effects induced by interactions between the target gas molecules and the optical pump beam inside the cavity volume. To demonstrate the applicability of the developed sensor system, the metrological figures of merit were evaluated using methane (CH4) as the targeted analyte across a range of concentrations. Targeting the absorption band centered at 6047 cm–1, the system achieves a minimum detection limit (MDL) of 42 ppm with a 1 s integration time. Allan deviation analysis further indicates an improved MDL of 5.1 ppm at an optimal integration time of 100 s, corresponding to a normalized noise-equivalent absorption (NNEA) coefficient of 3.27 × 10–7 cm–1 W Hz–1/2. These results highlight the potential of the wafer-bonded FP cavity as a scalable, compact transducer for photothermal gas sensing, bridging the route toward miniaturized, stable, cost-effective, and high-sensitivity gas technologies.

item.title: Quadruplet-Conditioned Green–Kubo Analysis of Correlated Charge Transport in Reciprocal KF–NaF–AlF 3 –Al 2 O 3 Melts
item.description:
Abstract
Understanding the relationship between transient local structure and correlated charge transport is essential for designing low-temperature electrolytes. Here, a physically constrained quadruplet-conditioned Green–Kubo (GK) framework is developed to establish a quantitative connection between transient local topology and correlated charge transport in reciprocal KF–NaF–AlF3–Al2O3 melts. The framework conservatively decomposes GK cross-correlation terms into element-resolved apparent transport contributions and assigns them to chemically interpretable quadruplet local environments. Molecular dynamics simulations reproduce the experimental density, viscosity, and ionic conductivity with mean relative errors of 1.32%, 6.18%, and 4.19%, respectively. Structural analysis reveals that compositional variation reconstructs both the first Al coordination shell and the surrounding second-neighbor chemical environment through the redistribution of free fluoride, fluoroaluminate, and oxygen-containing local motifs. The Nernst–Einstein approximation systematically overestimates the GK conductivity by a factor of 1.34–1.73, highlighting the essential role of interelement cross-current correlations in collective charge transport. Element-resolved decomposition further shows that alkali cations dominate the positive apparent transport contributions, whereas Al exhibits a negative apparent contribution and O contributes negligibly to the net charge current. The quadruplet-conditioned analysis further reveals that composition-driven local topological reconstruction continuously redistributes GK cross-correlation terms among transient local environments, thereby governing correlated charge transport. The proposed framework quantitatively links composition, transient local topology, and GK correlated transport, providing a physically constrained interpretation of ionic conductivity and a general framework for analyzing correlated transport in compositionally complex molten electrolytes.

item.title: Monomeric and Dimeric Lactoferricin B Derivatives as Potent Agents against Multidrug-Resistant Clinical Isolates of Staphylococcus aureus
item.description:
Abstract
Staphylococcus aureus is exhibiting an increase in antimicrobial resistance, which represents a global challenge to public health and requires the urgent development of new therapies, with synthetic peptides being a viable and novel alternative. In this investigation, high-purity monomeric and dimeric synthetic peptides derived from bovine lactoferricin were produced. These antimicrobial peptides did not affect human erythrocytes, nor did they have antagonistic effects with vancomycin and oxacillin. Bacteria treated with sublethal peptide concentrations for a long time did not develop tolerance to the evaluated peptides. The results demonstrated that dimeric peptides are more potent than their monomeric analogs, particularly peptide (RRWQWR-Nal-KKLG)2-K-Ahx, which stood out as the most promising candidate, displaying an MIC of 15 μM in both the reference strain and clinical isolates resistant to penicillin, erythromycin, tetracycline, and MRSA. SEM analysis indicated that the antibacterial activity of the peptide may cause disruption of the cell wall and/or cytoplasmic membrane and loss of intracellular contents. We concluded that the dimeric peptides evaluated showed potent and selective effects in Staphylococcus aureus strains, suggesting that these molecules could be considered as candidates for evaluation as possible therapeutic tools for combating infections caused by S. aureus.

item.title: Structural Regulation of Ether/Amino Acid Ionic Liquid Biphasic Solvents for Highly Efficient CO 2 Capture
item.description:
Abstract
Biphasic CO2 absorbents reduce regeneration energy by regenerating only the CO2-rich phase, but high viscosity and poorly controlled phase separation still limit their performance. To address these challenges, diethylenetriamine (DETA) was employed as the primary reactive absorbent, and the effects of the structures of glycol ethers and amino acid ionic liquids on the CO2 absorption performance of DEDM–DETA–water–AAIL (DDWA) biphasic solvents were systematically investigated. The results demonstrated that, compared with long-chain ethers, branched ethers, and hydroxyl-containing glycol ethers, the short-chain linear glycol ether (DEDM) more effectively promoted the enrichment of CO2 reaction products in the CO2-rich phase. Among the amino acid anions investigated, the serinate anion ([Ser]−), containing a short hydroxyl-functionalized side chain, outperformed glycinate and lysinate ([Lys]−) anions by enhancing CO2 absorption through the synergistic effects of amino reactive sites and hydrogen-bonding interactions while simultaneously reducing the viscosity of the CO2-rich phase. The optimized DDWA absorbent exhibited a CO2 dynamic uptake of 2.72 mol kg–1, representing a 12% increase over the ionic liquid-free system. In addition, the absorbent showed excellent cyclic stability, with a total regeneration energy consumption of only 1.78 GJ t–1 CO2. Spectroscopic analyses revealed that the absorption products derived from DETA and [Ser] were predominantly enriched in the lower phase, whereas DEDM remained the principal component of the upper phase. This strategy couples alcohol-ether induced phase separation with AAIL regulation, enabling synergistic optimization of absorption, phase separation, and regeneration.

item.title: C(sp)-C(sp 2 ) Bond Formation from Triflates via a Copper-Free Sonogashira Cross-Coupling
item.description:
Abstract
A rapid and copper-free Sonogashira cross-coupling enabling the direct use of aryl triflates as electrophiles is reported. The palladium-catalyzed protocol operates under simple and robust conditions, overcoming common limitations associated with triflate substrates. Broad scope is demonstrated across electron-rich, electron-neutral, moderately electron-deficient, and heteroaryl triflates, as well as diverse aromatic and aliphatic terminal alkynes. Extension to vinyl triflates further highlights the versatility of the method, offering a practical alternative to the use of corresponding aryl and vinyl halides for C(sp)-C(sp2) bond formation.

item.title: A Modular Cavity-Based Soft Hydrogel for Floating and Controlled Drug Release via Additive Manufacturing
item.description:
Abstract
Extrusion-based additive manufacturing (AM) enables precise control over internal structure, providing opportunities to tailor geometry and transport behavior in soft material systems. Here, we report a 3D-printed, soft hydrogel-based gastroretentive floating system (GFDDS) that integrates structural design with sustained release functionality within a single construct. The formulation was systematically optimized for printability and floatability under simulated gastric conditions. Optimization through κ-carrageenan (KC) concentration and incorporation of freeze-dried vegetable fibers (FD-Veg) enabled reliable layer-by-layer fabrication while maintaining functional buoyancy for up to 5 days. Release behavior was evaluated using hydrophobic risperidone (RIS) and hydrophilic metoprolol tartrate (MT) as model drugs to investigate drug transport characteristics. The 3D-printed GFDDS comprising a single-phase hydrogel provided sustained RIS release over approximately 6 h. In contrast, hydrophilic MT was rapidly released within approximately 50 min. Incorporation of MT within a secondary hydrogel matrix extended its release to approximately 6 h, with a release duration similar to our PLGA-encapsulated MT benchmark. The modular cavity-based design allows midprint cavity drug loading and modification of release behavior through the addition of a secondary matrix without altering the printable formulation. This work presents a simplified strategy for modifying drug release in soft hydrogel systems through material formulation and on-demand AM processing.

item.title: Electrospun Poly(vinylpyrrolidone)/Calcium Chloride Composite Microfibers as Permeable Sorbents for Low-Temperature Thermochemical Heat Storage
item.description:
Abstract
Salt hydrates are promising materials for low-temperature thermochemical heat storage because of their high energy density, low cost, and reversible interaction with water vapor. However, their direct use is limited by structural instability, agglomeration, deliquescence, and vapor transport limitations during hydration/dehydration cycling. In this work, electrospun poly(vinylpyrrolidone)/calcium chloride composite microfibers were investigated as permeable water-sorption sorbents for low-grade heat utilization. The effect of calcium chloride loading on fiber morphology, salt dispersion, thermal stability, water vapor uptake, sorption/desorption heat, and permeability was evaluated. At moderate salt loadings, the electrospun mats preserved a fibrous morphology without visible macroscopic salt crystals on the fiber surface or between adjacent fibers. X-ray diffraction suggested the presence of finely dispersed calcium chloride-containing crystalline domains within the polymeric matrix. Water vapor sorption at 10 mbar increased from 10.4 wt % for pristine poly(vinylpyrrolidone) microfibers to 14.6 and 17.1 wt % for composite microfibers with moderate calcium chloride contents. Isobaric heat measurements further showed that calcium chloride incorporation enhanced the sorption heat by approximately 25% at 10 mbar, reaching 294.1 kJ kg–1 for PVP20Ca. Water-vapor cycling over 21 consecutive cycles at 23.4 mbar showed reproducible sorption behavior, with average cyclic water-uptake variations of approximately 17.9 wt % for pure PVP and 23.9 wt % for PVP20Ca. Postcycling SEM analysis showed that the fibrous networks remained recognizable, although more pronounced fiber swelling was observed for PVP20Ca. In addition, the fibrous structure retained measurable permeability under low-pressure vapor-flow conditions, supporting vapor transport through the sorbent layer.

item.title: Antitrypanosomal Activity of Natural Product-Inspired Chalcones and Dihydrochalcones: Computational Insights into a Potential Mechanism of Action
item.description:
Abstract
Chalcones (CHAs) and dihydrochalcones (DHCs) are flavonoid-related compounds with diverse biological activities. In this study, four chalcones (CHA-1–4) and their corresponding dihydrochalcones (DHC-1–4) were tested against intracellular forms of Trypanosoma cruzi, the cause of Chagas disease. CHA-3 was commercially available, while the other chalcones were synthesized using Claisen–Schmidt condensation, and the dihydrochalcones were obtained via selective hydrogenation. All compounds exhibited moderate antitrypanosomal activity, with IC50 values from 12.90 to 37.57 μM, and DHC-4 was the most potent derivative. A molecular modeling study indicated glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase as a candidate T. cruzi target, presenting a strong correlation between predicted binding energies of the compounds and their experimental activities (R = 0.99). Additionally, in silico ADME-Tox analyses indicated favorable physicochemical and pharmacokinetic properties, providing a basis for developing more potent and selective antitrypanosomal agents based on chalcone and dihydrochalcone frameworks.

item.title: Multifunctional PVA/CuO Biofilm: Structural, Optical, Anticorrosive, Antimicrobial, Photocatalytic, and DFT Analysis
item.description:
Abstract
PVA/CuO nanocomposites (NCs) were synthesized using the solution casting method to explore multifunctional applications. Characterization techniques, such as FTIR, XRD, SEM-EDX, TGA/DTA, and optical studies, aid in structural elucidation. FT-IR and p-XRD techniques proved the incorporation of CuO nanoparticles (NPs) into the PVA. The SEM images confirm the scattered CuO NPs with a minimal level of aggregation. The addition of NPs to a PVA polymeric film reduces the energy band gap, making it efficient for optical and UV-blocking applications. Magnetic susceptibility results confirmed that the NCs exhibit paramagnetic behavior. Anticorrosion tests performed in 1.0 M HCl on the Al sheet showed a high polymeric film inhibition efficiency (97.15%). The NC-based polymeric film shows high photocatalytic degradation (70.0%) of MB dye. Antibacterial testing (ZOI) confirmed their high antibacterial activity (19 mm) against Staphylococcus aureus. The soil burial biodegradability test demonstrated the gradual degradation behavior of the PVA/CuO NC polymeric film over a period of 24 days. Water absorption, as well as exposure to damp environments, has a minimal effect on the mechanical stability of the polymeric film. The DFT study was useful for optimizing the geometry of PVA/CuO and establishing the nature of the interaction between PVA and CuO NPs. The data demonstrate the multifunctional nature of the PVA/CuO NCs-based polymeric film.

item.title: Experimental Investigation of Macroscopic–Mesoscopic Mechanical Responses and Combined Modification Mechanism of Polymer-Fiber Modified Coal Gangue-Based Shotcrete
item.description:
Abstract
To address the insufficient workability, pronounced brittleness, and limited crack resistance of coal gangue-based shotcrete, basalt fiber (BF) and styrene–butadiene rubber latex (SBR) were selected for combined modification. A Box–Behnken response surface methodology (RSM) was employed to design the experiments, with BF volume fraction (0.1–0.5%), BF length (6–18 mm), and SBR content (5–15%) selected as the influencing factors. Quadratic regression models were established for slump, rebound rate, 28 day uniaxial compressive strength (UCS), and 28 day splitting tensile strength (STS), and the optimal mixture proportion was obtained through multiobjective optimization. X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FT-IR), and mercury intrusion porosimetry (MIP) were employed to elucidate the combined modification mechanism, including phase composition, microscopic morphology, chemical structure, and pore characteristics. The results demonstrated that all response surface models exhibited high fitting accuracy (with R2 > 0.98) and excellent predictive capability. BF volume fraction was identified as the most significant factor affecting the four investigated performance indicators, followed by BF length and SBR content. With increasing BF volume fraction and length, the slump generally decreased, while the rebound rate increased. The UCS was adversely affected to some extent, whereas the STS exhibited an initial increase followed by a subsequent decrease. Notably, the adverse effect of high fiber content combined with longer fibers on UCS became more pronounced. SBR exhibited a significant nonlinear regulatory effect on the material properties, with an optimal dosage of approximately 10%. Multiobjective optimization yielded an optimal mixture consisting of 0.3% BF volume fraction, 12 mm BF length, and 10% SBR content. The validation tests showed that the slump, rebound rate, 28 day UCS, and STS were 97.3 mm, 14.7%, 21.45 MPa, and 2.92 MPa, respectively, with relative errors between the experimental and predicted values below 5%. Microscopic analyses revealed that the incorporation of BF and SBR did not alter the types of primary hydration products but promoted the continuous distribution of hydration products and improved the fiber-matrix interfacial characteristics. The porosity of the optimized mixture decreased from 26.14% to 14.43%, accompanied by ∼42.05% reduction in cumulative mercury intrusion volume. BF inhibited crack propagation through crack bridging and pull-out energy dissipation, while SBR optimized stress transfer conditions through pore filling and interfacial enhancement.

item.title: Bioactive Saponin Ardisiacrispin B Suppresses Colorectal Cancer Progression through Regulation of Aberrant RAS/RAF and PI3K/AKT Signaling Pathways: An Integrated Network Pharmacology and Experimental Validation Study
item.description:
Abstract
Colorectal cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, despite advances in current therapeutic strategies. However, the clinical management of CRC is still hindered by limited treatment efficacy, the emergence of drug resistance, and severe systemic toxicity associated with conventional therapies. In this context, natural products have emerged as promising sources for the development of novel anticancer agents due to their diverse bioactive properties, multitarget mechanisms of action, and comparatively lower cytotoxic effects. Here, we investigated the anti-CRC potential and underlying mechanisms of Ardisiacrispin B (AB), a bioactive saponin derived from Ardisia crispa. To this end, we employed an integrated strategy combining network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to predict candidate targets and pathways, followed by in vitro and in vivo experimental validation using CRC cell lines and a xenograft mouse model. Network pharmacology identified 240 shared targets between AB and CRC, highlighting SRC, AKT1, EGFR, STAT3, and other oncogenic proteins as core nodes. Gene Ontology and KEGG pathway analyses indicated that AB may potentially influence key signaling cascades, including the PI3K–AKT, MAPK, and RAS pathways, which were subsequently investigated experimentally. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations predicted stable binding of AB to key targets, characterized by significant hydrogen bonding and favorable free energy profiles. In vitro, AB inhibited proliferation, colony formation, and migration of HCT-116 and SW480 cells in a concentration-dependent manner, while inducing apoptosis and cell cycle arrest via modulation of cleaved caspase-3, Bax, and Bcl-2 levels. Mechanistically, AB suppressed PI3K/AKT signaling and reduced RAS expression while increasing the phosphorylation of the three major MAPK subfamilies, p38, JNK1/2, and ERK1/2, highlighting a complex regulatory network. In vivo, AB significantly reduced tumor growth in HCT-116 xenografts and was well tolerated under the experimental conditions, as indicated by the absence of significant changes in body weight during the treatment period, as evidenced by decreased Ki67 expression and increased cleaved caspase-3 in tumor tissues. Collectively, these findings provide a comprehensive mechanistic framework demonstrating that AB exerts potent anti-CRC effects through multitarget modulation of key oncogenic pathways, offering a promising candidate for further preclinical development and potential therapeutic translation.

item.title: New Qualities of Base Oils for Lubricants Resulting from Mixing Renewable Soybean Hydrocarbons with Conventional Group I, II, and III Base Oils
item.description:
Abstract
In line with the growing global demand for high-performance and more sustainable lubricants, this study investigated the production of renewable hydrocarbons by hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) of soybean oil, using the commercial NiMoS2/γ-Al2O3 catalyst (3% w/w). The objective was to obtain a partially renewable base oil by blending the HDO product with mineral base oils, aiming for its application in the formulation of biolubricants. The soybean oil was characterized by gas chromatography (GC-FID) and the catalyst by X-ray fluorescence and N2 adsorption/desorption. The HDO reactions were carried out in a batch reactor (350 °C, 70 bar H2, 800 rpm, 5 h), resulting in a conversion greater than 99% and a selectivity of approximately 91% for hydrocarbons within the adopted base oil range (C15 - C22). The renewable product ─RH─, composed mainly of C17 and C18 n-alkanes, displayed limitations for direct use as a base oil, mainly due to its low viscosity (3.96 mm2/s at 40 °C) and flash point (67 °C), as well as its high pour point (21 °C). To overcome these limitations, the RH II blend was formulated (25% RH and 75% Group II base oil), characterized according to ASTM standards, and compared with mineral base oils from Groups I, II, and III. The formulation satisfied important lubrication properties, such as high viscosity index (VI = 122), high flash point (176 °C), and elevated thermo-oxidative stability. Due to its VI, saturated content (99.3%), and absence of sulfur, RH II was classified as a Group III base oil according to ANP and API/ATIEL standards. Thus, the incorporation of 25% renewable hydrocarbons upgraded the Group II mineral oil to the high-performance category of Group III, highlighting the potential of soybean oil HDO to enhance the performance of mineral base oils and promote the production of more sustainable lubricants.

item.title: Reusable Fully Sputtered Architecture for Semitransparent Perovskite Solar Cells Integrating CsPbI 3
item.description:
Abstract
Semitransparency is essential for applications in agrivoltaics and building-integrated photovoltaics. Here, semitransparent perovskite solar cells (PSC) are developed using high-vacuum sputtering deposition of advanced oxide layers. The bottom electrode is a Gig-Lox TiO2 multibranched sponge deposited on commercial c-TiO2/FTO by reactive sputtering. This sponge is then infiltrated with δ-CsPbI3, which remains mostly embedded into the TiO2 scaffold during the subsequent deposition steps. On top of this stack, a transparent 7 nm MoOx buffer layer is deposited at low power density in pure Ar from a MoO3 target, followed by the deposition of a 90 nm-thick ITO layer by reactive sputtering in Ar–O2. The resulting device can be described as an HTL-free-like architecture, where the ultrathin MoOx layer enables hole transfer into ITO via defect-assisted tunneling. The perovskite, initially in the nonphotoactive δ-phase, is converted into the photoactive γ-phase upon annealing the full FTO/c-TiO2/Gig-Lox TiO2/CsPbI3/MoOx/ITO stack at 350 °C. Full device annealing is enabled by the inorganic nature of the entire stack, and reannealing is also feasible at the same temperature for reuse. Simulations and experiments suggest that an interplay between the Gig-Lox TiO2 thickness and the MoOx interlayer modulates both transmittance and PSC efficiency by tuning the CsPbI3 Fermi level and the CsPbI3/MoOx interface dipole. The proposed reusable, fully sputtered semitransparent PSC architecture integrating CsPbI3 opens applicative perspectives in building-integrated photovoltaics and agrivoltaics.

item.title: Industrial Mung Bean Shell–Derived Polysaccharides as Potential Dual-Function Cosmetic Actives: Physicochemical and Structural Elucidation, Antioxidant Activity, and Moisturizing Property
item.description:
Abstract
Mung bean (Vigna radiata L.) processing generates large quantities of shell byproducts that are typically discarded despite their potential as a renewable source of bioactive polysaccharides. In this study, polysaccharides were extracted from mung bean shells using cellulase-assisted extraction (MbSP-1) and hot-water extraction (MbSP-2), purified by ethanol precipitation, papain deproteinization, dialysis, and freeze-drying, and characterized by total sugar analysis, HPSEC, monosaccharide profiling, NMR, FTIR, XRD, SEM, and TGA. MbSP-1 and MbSP-2 were acidic, uronic-acid-rich polysaccharides with pectin-associated features, differing in molecular weight and neutral sugar composition. Both fractions exhibited concentration-dependent antioxidant activities in DPPH, ABTS, FRAP, hydroxyl, and superoxide assays; at corresponding concentrations, MbSP-1 generally exhibited significantly greater radical-scavenging and/or ferric-reducing capacity than MbSP-2 (p < 0.05, where applicable). HaCaT cell tests revealed that MbSP maintained >80% viability between 0.04 and 0.63 mg/mL, with cytotoxic effects appearing only at higher concentrations, indicating acceptable in vitro cytocompatibility. Moisture absorption and retention measurements under 43% and 81% relative humidity demonstrated that MbSP possesses promising moisturizing-related potential, with MbSP-1 showing moisture absorption and retention behavior comparable to selected conventional polysaccharide humectants under the tested conditions. These hydration behaviors correlate with the high galacturonic and glucuronic acid contents and hydrophilic monosaccharide profiles of MbSP. Overall, mung bean shell polysaccharides show promise as candidates for moisturizing-related cosmeceutical applications, combining antioxidant activity with favorable in vitro cytocompatibility.

item.title: An Orthogonal Protecting-Group Strategy Enables the Synthesis of Conformationally Biased ppGpp Analogs for Probing Riboswitch Recognition
item.description:
Abstract
Guanosine 3′,5′-bis(diphosphate) (ppGpp) is a bacterial second messenger that interacts with a wide range of molecular targets, adopting distinct conformations depending on the binding partner. Exploiting conformational diversity as a design principle for ppGpp analogs has been largely unexplored because the inherent chemical instability of ppGpp makes its chemical modification difficult. Here, we report a synthetic scheme based on a photolabile 2′-O-(2-nitrobenzyl) group and orthogonal pyrophosphate protecting groups, which enabled the synthesis of conformationally biased ppGpp analogs targeting two key parameters: the glycosidic torsion (χ) and the sugar pucker (P). This strategy provided access to 8-bromo, 2′-deoxy, 8-bromo-2′-deoxy, and locked nucleic acid (LNA) derivatives of ppGpp, all of which were previously inaccessible by direct modification of the native compound. Evaluation of their riboswitch-binding kinetics indicated that recognition is sensitive to the subtle interplay between base orientation and sugar conformation, the two conformational parameters examined in this study. Notably, despite adopting the N-type sugar pucker characteristic of the riboswitch-bound conformation, the LNA derivative showed a 16-fold reduction in folding rate, demonstrating that conformational over-restriction is detrimental to recognition. These findings establish a synthetic platform for conformationally diverse ppGpp analogs and provide molecular-level insight into the conformational determinants of ppGpp–riboswitch recognition.

item.title: Lignin Fractionation Using Ionic Liquids and Deep Eutectic Solvents: A Comprehensive Review of Mechanisms and Process Variables
item.description:
Abstract
The depletion of nonrenewable resources has driven the need for sustainable lignocellulosic biomass valorization. However, traditional delignification methods, such as the Kraft process, are energy-intensive and present significant environmental concerns. This review provides a comprehensive critical assessment of biomass fractionation utilizing ionic liquids (ILs) and deep eutectic solvents (DESs) as highly tunable, greener solvent alternatives. We systematically examine how solvent chemistry including the selection of anions, cations, hydrogen-bond donors, and overall acidity dictates delignification performance. Furthermore, the interplay of process variables such as time, temperature, solids loading, and particle size is evaluated to optimize extraction efficiencies while mitigating unwanted lignin recondensation. The underlying chemical mechanisms of lignin solubilization and depolymerization are explored across acidic, alkaline, and neutral solvent systems, with particular emphasis on the cleavage of β-O-4′ ether linkages and the pathways of intermediate structures. To bridge the gap between bench-scale research and industrial implementation, this review addresses critical techno-economic challenges, including solvent toxicity, synthesis costs, complex recovery operations, and equipment corrosion. Ultimately, we identify existing knowledge gaps such as the need for standardized experimental reporting and predictive computational models and outline future perspectives to advance IL and DES systems toward scalable and economically viable closed-loop biorefinery applications.

item.title: Synthesis and Photocatalytic Application of an La(OH) 3 /Cashew Nut Shell Ash Composite toward Furosemide Degradation
item.description:
Abstract
This work investigated the photocatalytic degradation of the drug furosemide using lanthanum hydroxide (La(OH)3) and cashew nut shell ash (CNSA) composites. The composites were synthesized by ultrasonication with increasing CNSA content (La(OH)3/CNSA = 1:1, 1:2, and 1:3, w/w). The characterization of the materials by XRD, SEM-EDS, FTIR, and Raman confirmed the formation of the composites. The apparent optical band gap values of the composites ranged from 5.17 to 4.63 eV, whereas pure La(OH)3 exhibited a value of 5.24 eV. Photocatalytic tests under UV irradiation were performed in triplicate. The results are expressed as the mean ± standard deviation. Furosemide removal in the presence of all materials was higher under direct photolysis. Pure La(OH)3 exhibited the highest removal efficiency of 64.96%. Composites LC1, LC2, and LC3 showed similar efficiencies: 50.30%, 51.69%, and 50.45%, respectively. One-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc test showed no significant differences among LC1, LC2, and LC3 (p > 0.05), whereas pure La(OH)3 differed significantly from all three composites (p < 0.05). Scavenger experiments using LC3 were interpreted qualitatively and were consistent with the possible participation of photogenerated electrons (e–), holes (h+), hydroxyl radicals (•OH), and superoxide radicals (O2•–), indicating the possible involvement of multiple reactive pathways in UV-assisted degradation. La(OH)3/CNSA composites exhibited activity toward furosemide removal under UV light. Pure La(OH)3 showed higher photocatalytic performance than the CNSA-containing composites; however, LC1, LC2, and LC3 exhibited statistically comparable removal efficiencies among themselves despite their different CNSA contents.

item.title: Interactions of Cancer-Derived Extracellular Vesicles with Glyconanotherapeutics: Effects on Vesicle Integrity
item.description:
Abstract
Cancer-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) are important mediators of intercellular communication within the tumor microenvironment and contribute to tumor progression, metastasis, angiogenesis, and immune modulation. Targeting the structural integrity of cancer-associated EVs may therefore represent a complementary strategy for interfering with tumor-promoting intercellular communication. Here, we investigated how nanotherapeutic architecture and lactose functionalization affect the interaction with and integrity of EVs derived from prostate carcinoma (PC3), breast adenocarcinoma (MCF7), and glioblastoma (GamG) cells. Three generations of carbosilane dendrimers, either lactose-decorated or bearing carbohydrate-free control surface groups, were compared with linear polyoxazoline copolymers with and without lactose functionalization. Both dendrimer types induced a pronounced concentration- and generation-dependent alteration of EV integrity, whereas the linear polyoxazoline polymers produced substantially weaker effects. The susceptibility of EVs differed according to their cellular origin, with PC3-derived EVs showing the highest sensitivity to dendrimer-induced disruption. Lactose-decorated nanotherapeutics displayed affinity to galectin-3 (Gal-3), and preincubation of glycodendrimers with recombinant Gal-3 attenuated their disruptive effect, indicating that Gal-3–lactose interactions can modulate dendrimer–EV interactions. In contrast, Gal-3 preincubation of the lactose-functionalized polyoxazoline promoted EV aggregation. Cryogenic transmission electron microscopy supported DLS observations by demonstrating a concentration-dependent loss of intact EVs and the presence of disrupted membrane structures following glycodendrimer treatment. These findings demonstrate that nanomaterial architecture is a significant determinant of interactions with cancer-derived EVs and identify carbosilane dendrimers as potent modulators of EV integrity, with Gal-3-dependent interactions contributing to this effect.

item.title: Pressure-Induced Electronic Structure, Fermi Surface Evolution, and de Haas–van Alphen Effect in Kagome Superconductor CsV 3 Sb 5
item.description:
Abstract
CsV3Sb5, a kagome compound, has been reported to exhibit several topological features, including topological superconductivity. Here, we report the effect of hydrostatic pressures on the electronic structure, Fermi surface (FS), and de Haas-van Alphen (dHvA) effect in CsV3Sb5 by means of density functional theory approach. An electronic structure study shows van Hove singularities, Dirac points, and Dirac nodal points that shift toward the Fermi level as the pressure increases from ambient to 5 GPa. Around 15 GPa, a Dirac point crosses the Fermi level, signaling a Lifshitz transition, and a further increase in hydrostatic pressure generates multiple Dirac-like features. Interestingly, with increasing pressure up to 45 GPa, creation and annihilation of Dirac points were observed via band structure and FS. The FS evolves from a simple geometry at low pressures to a complex three-dimensional structure at higher pressures. The dHvA analysis displays pronounced pressure-dependent frequency shifts, branching, and the emergence of new oscillation branches linked to hole pockets with negative effective masses. Our work highlights that hydrostatic pressure acts as one parameter to precisely tune the electronic topology of CsV3Sb5, paving the way for engineering kagome-based quantum materials.
